title: 629. Great Leaders Let the Customer Set the Agenda
author: The Business Leader Daily
summary: This Business Leader Daily piece argues that customer expectations are a constantly moving target, and that most leaders overestimate how well they're meeting them -- citing a Bain survey where 80 percent of companies believed they delivered a superior experience while only 8 percent of their customers agreed. It contrasts reactive leadership with customer-centric leaders who build curiosity, experimentation, and fast feedback into their organizations so they can anticipate shifts before customers voice them, closing with a curated set of quotes on customer-centricity from business leaders and authors.
points: Cites a Bain survey of 362 companies: 80 percent believed they delivered a superior customer experience, but only 8 percent of their customers agreed.
Argues satisfaction has a short shelf life -- customers are trained by ongoing progress to expect continuous improvement, not stasis.
Distinguishes reactive leaders, who respond to complaints, from customer-centric leaders, who build curiosity and fast feedback loops to anticipate needs eighteen months out.
Closes with a curated set of quotes on customer focus from figures including Jeff Bezos, A.G. Lafley, and Frank Blake.
quotes: Bain surveyed 362 companies and found that 80 percent believed they were delivering a superior experience.
Customers are not sitting still, waiting for you to catch up.
The complaint nobody bothers to file is often the most expensive one in the business.
The advantage belongs to the leader who sees the shift while it is still small.
The customer decides what matters. The work is staying close enough to hear the verdict early.
Most companies assume they are consistently giving customers what they want. Usually, they are kidding themselves.
